cma:2025.271.name: Unidentified Merina-style weaver
cma:2025.271.detail: The catalogue describes the silk wrapper, its weft-float pattern, and a wider comparison for the knotted fringe.

cma:2013.5.name: Mbuun-style weavers
cma:2013.5.role: Catalogue role in making the panels
cma:2013.5.detail: The museum describes Mbuun men weaving skirts that women wore.

cma:2013.5.name: Mbuun-style embroiderers
cma:2013.5.role: Catalogue role in finishing the panels
cma:2013.5.detail: The museum identifies an embroidered border and shorter fibres crossing the joins.

cma:2003.89.name: Dida-style weavers and dyers
cma:2003.89.detail: The museum describes a raffia wrapper with knot-and-twist resist dyeing. Tying helps account for the crinkled surface.

cma:2024.72.name: Unidentified Fulani-style wool weavers
cma:2024.72.detail: The catalogue describes a wool cover made from six handwoven strips joined along their selvages.

cma:2003.86.name: Unidentified Tétouan weavers
cma:2003.86.detail: The museum describes a silk brocade grid with navy and crimson faces and connects msimsim hangings to recorded marriage gifts in Tétouan.

cma:1916.1229.name: Unidentified Algerian weaver and embroiderer
cma:1916.1229.detail: The museum describes an Algerian curtain with two surviving embroidered widths and joined ribbons. It says a third width is missing.

cma:1916.1361.name: Unidentified Djerba weavers
cma:1916.1361.detail: The pair’s record distinguishes woven silk bands from embroidery.

cma:1916.1361.name: Unidentified Djerba embroiderers
cma:1916.1361.detail: The museum identifies gold-thread embroidery and distinguishes specialist roles on Djerba.

met:91.1.53.name: Unidentified scarf maker
met:91.1.53.detail: The Met catalogues this late eighteenth-century wool piece as a scarf end, 24.1 by 76.2 centimetres.

met:09.160.name: Unidentified damask weaver
met:09.160.detail: The Met lists joined damask silk and records the whole hanging at 217.2 by 173.4 centimetres.

cma:1995.210.name: Unidentified female potter
cma:1995.210.detail: The museum describes the potter joining two bowls and adding a neck before detailing the surface.

cma:1975.1011.name: Unidentified Lobi-style basket maker
cma:1975.1011.detail: The catalogue groups ten nesting baskets and a stopper. It gives separate dimensions for the graduated parts.

cma:1929.326.name: Unidentified Mangbetu-style basket maker
cma:1929.326.detail: The record calls this object a basket and measures the top at 31.6 centimetres across. A catalogue note calls it a hat and connects it to visitors passing through Ekibondo.

cma:1915.460.name: Unidentified maker of the jug and strap
cma:1915.460.detail: The accession groups a terracotta water jug with a separate plant-fibre carrying strap.

walters:41.45.name: Unidentified Egyptian stoneworker
walters:41.45.detail: The museum gives separate top and base diameters for the small Egyptian vase and identifies a rounded bottom in the object title.

met:17.194.1812.name: Unidentified lamp maker
met:17.194.1812.detail: The Met records molded earthenware from Utica and lists three dimensions for this lamp.

met:89.4.553.name: Unidentified Malagasy instrument maker
met:89.4.553.detail: The Met catalogues a bamboo-and-wood marovany, 124.5 centimetres long and 7.6 centimetres across.

walters:48.2044.name: Unidentified Cypriot potter
walters:48.2044.detail: The museum identifies the sideways barrel form as work of a Cypriot potter.

walters:48.2044.name: Estate of Mrs. Samuel C. Lamport
walters:48.2044.detail: The Walters records the estate’s gift in 1952, separate from the object’s Iron Age date.

walters:54.776.name: Unidentified Greek bronze worker
walters:54.776.detail: The Walters identifies this bronze piece as an attachment where the handle met the rim of a water jug.

walters:47.6.name: al-Walid ibn Abdul-Rahman
walters:47.6.detail: The museum records this name under Patron for the pound weight.

walters:47.6.name: Yazid III
walters:47.6.detail: The museum identifies this name in its account of the stamped inscription.

walters:54.2434.name: Unidentified maker, with Egyptian and Italian attributions considered
walters:54.2434.detail: The Walters identifies an animal-shaped bronze pouring vessel and keeps Egyptian and Italian maker attributions open.

walters:57.586.name: Unidentified metalworker
walters:57.586.detail: The catalogue allows two possible places of origin for the granulated work.

walters:57.586.name: Henry Walters
walters:57.586.detail: The provenance records his 27 September 1913 purchase and the 1931 bequest.

walters:71.48.name: Unidentified Sicilian maker
walters:71.48.detail: The catalogue identifies the origin and traces two decorated faces.

walters:71.48.name: Unidentified repairer
walters:71.48.detail: The museum describes a repaired break and gives no date for that repair.

nmafa:89-13-73.name: Unidentified potter
nmafa:89-13-73.detail: The Smithsonian links the form with a pottery tradition and gives no individual maker.

nmafa:89-13-73.name: Walshaert collection
nmafa:89-13-73.detail: Antwerp before 1930 appears in the provenance field.

met:1991.17.18.name: Ìgùn Ẹ́rọ̀nwwọ̀n artists
met:1991.17.18.detail: The Met credits the guild of brass casters for the plaque.

met:1991.17.18.name: Two Portuguese merchants
met:1991.17.18.detail: Their role comes from the museum title and sculpture account, separate from maker attribution.

met:08.202.26a-b.name: Unidentified silver workers
met:08.202.26a-b.detail: The Met records two numbered silver pendants under one accession and retains a probable Moroccan geographical attribution.

met:04.34.9.name: Unidentified goldworker
met:04.34.9.detail: The Met describes the material and a geographical attribution.

met:04.34.9.name: Meredith Howland
met:04.34.9.detail: The accession credit identifies a gift in 1904.

met:08.180.957.name: Unidentified lace maker
met:08.180.957.detail: The record uses the term bobbin lace but gives no named maker.

met:08.180.957.name: Mrs. Magdalena Nuttall
met:08.180.957.detail: The collection credit names her gift in 1908. The gift record is separate from the making date.

walters:48.2036.name: Unidentified Egyptian potter
walters:48.2036.detail: The Walters catalogue identifies glazed earthenware with luster decoration and describes yellow-golden painting around a central bird.

walters:73.106.name: Unidentified Egyptian leather worker
walters:73.106.detail: The Walters records paint on red-stained parchment or alum-tawed hide. The description leaves a possible book-cover function open because no backing is preserved.

walters:42.109.name: Gnaios
walters:42.109.role: Name inscribed on the gem according to the Walters
walters:42.109.detail: The museum reads the vertically engraved name of a late first-century BCE gem-carver.

walters:42.109.name: Polykleitos
walters:42.109.role: Proposed link to a possible sculptural model
walters:42.109.detail: The account mentions that an older statue by a follower could have informed the small scene. The two dates and roles stay separate.

cma:1915.453.name: Unidentified Chokwe-style maker
cma:1915.453.detail: The Cleveland record lists wood, glass beads and natural fibres. Its account says the wide teeth helped hold elements of a hairstyle.

cma:1915.452.name: Unidentified Luba-style maker
cma:1915.452.detail: The Cleveland record lists wood and wire for this small comb and gives an approximate date.

met:23.67.1.name: Unidentified maker of the glazed tile
met:23.67.1.detail: The Met lists stonepaste and glaze for this tile and gives a depth of 2.2 centimetres.

met:09.50.2779.name: Unidentified scarf weaver and embroiderer
met:09.50.2779.detail: The Met identifies this scarf as linen and silk, with plain weaving and embroidery.

nmafa:2010-10-30.name: Unidentified Akan artist
nmafa:2010-10-30.detail: The Smithsonian describes a copper-alloy saawa with concentric incisions in its bowl. The account explains that this type of spoon transferred gold dust to a scale.

met:1983.143.name: Middle Niger catalogue attribution
met:1983.143.detail: The Met records bronze for this Middle Niger bracelet and gives its diameter as 7.9 centimetres.
